name: Graphite
author: Peter Bednarčík. Colours from Visual Studio 2026 Dark theme data; structure from JetBrains' Islands Dark theme (Apache-2.0)
sourceNote: Visual Studio side: **Dark**, decoded from an installed Visual Studio 2026 by `tools/decode_vs_theme.py`. The token choices follow Morning Mist, where each was matched against screenshots of the Light-based theme; for Dark the values are decoded, not pixel-checked. Panel/header separation follows the Periwinkle Night clarity rules using this theme's own hue; those UI adjustments are marked designed, while the existing syntax palette is preserved.

layer-0-bg.element: Window frame and gaps: darker than the tool windows by the Islands minimum 1.20:1, in the panels' own hue

main-window-bg-alt.element: Alternate window background (Rider concept); uses the layered band

layer-0-border.element: Pane boundary in this theme's own palette; clearer than the inherited low-contrast separator

layer-0-border-inline.element: Inline borders on the window background

layer-1-bg.element: Dialog and settings-frame background. Measured in VS as the document-well header around the settings search box; its use for dialogs is by token name

layer-1-bg-inline.element: Input controls on a dialog: combo box and text field fill

layer-2-bg-inline.element: Inline areas inside popups (advertiser strip, headers)

editor-bg.element: Editor background. VS Dark leaves Plain Text background automatic (a built-in default), so it is absent from the theme data; 1E1E1E is the commonly used VS Dark editor colour, not a decoded value

editor-bg-inline.element: Inline editor chrome such as the in-editor search field

editor-border.element: Pane boundary in this theme's own palette; clearer than the inherited low-contrast separator

editor-border-inline.element: Pane boundary in this theme's own palette; clearer than the inherited low-contrast separator

editor-border-alt.element: Pane boundary in this theme's own palette; clearer than the inherited low-contrast separator

tool-window-bg.element: Tool pane body: separated from frame and unchanged editor in the theme's own hue

tool-window-border.element: Pane boundary in this theme's own palette; clearer than the inherited low-contrast separator

tool-window-border-inline.element: Pane boundary in this theme's own palette; clearer than the inherited low-contrast separator

text-default.element: Primary text. VS blends 000000 at alpha 228 over whatever is behind it; Rider needs one opaque colour, so it is blended over white

text-muted.element: Secondary text (Visual Studio's Cool Breeze overrides this token to alpha 178)

text-over-accent.element: Text on the accent colour (default button)

accent-brand-bg.element: Accent: selection pill, focused field underline, default button

accent-neutral-bg.element: Neutral badge and counter (the notification count)
accent-neutral-bg.contrastWaiver: the exact Visual Studio colour; Graphite is the faithful copy

core-bg-transparent-hovered.element: Hover fill on toolbar buttons and tabs (kept translucent, as in VS)

core-bg-transparent-pressed.element: Pressed fill. Fluent makes pressed lighter than hover

control-border.element: Border of buttons, combo boxes and text fields. VS draws a stronger bottom edge on text fields; Rider draws one colour on all four sides

control-border-small.element: Check box and radio button border

toolbar-selected-bg.element: Selected tool window button, window unfocused (Rider concept)

toolbar-selected-bg-active.element: Selected pill of a tool window's header tabs (Solution/Files) and of the Plugins dialog tabs. Rider keeps plain text on it, so a deeper shade of the accent: text on 9184EE was 2.5:1

toolbar-selected-bg-hovered.element: Hovered selected tool window button (Rider concept)

selection-bg-active.element: Selected row in trees and lists: SubtleFillSecondary over the tool window fill. The same token measures E7E7E7 over the settings page (F5F5F5) and C7D6DF over the tab well (D3E3ED) in VS. VS adds an accent pill at the left edge, which Rider cannot draw, so the selection is fainter here than it reads in VS

selection-bg-inactive.element: Selected row when the tree is not focused

tab-selected-bg-active.element: Selected document tab: same fill as the document

tab-selected-bg-inactive.element: Selected document tab in an unfocused group

popup-completion-match-text.element: Matched characters in the completion list

main-window-bg.element: Window frame and panel gaps use the frame layer, independently of dialog surfaces

tree-indent-guide-border.element: Visible hierarchy guides in this dark palette

MainToolbar.Dropdown.background.element: Pill on the title row (solution name in VS; project, branch and run widgets in Rider)

EditorTabs.background.element: Document tab well. With vertical tabs this is the fill of that panel in VS

MemoryIndicator.allocatedBackground.element: Memory indicator, allocated heap: the VS control fill on the band (the toolbar combo boxes in VS sample EEF4F8), so it stands out from the status bar

MemoryIndicator.usedBackground.element: Memory indicator, used heap: the hairline colour, darker than the allocated part

StatusBar.background.element: Status bar: Visual Studio's dark status bar. Unlike Morning Mist this works in Rider, which draws status bar icons light in a dark theme

EditorTabs.underlinedTabBackground.element: Selected document tab, fill. Visual Studio tints a selected document tab with the tab's colour at about 21 % over white and outlines it in that colour (sampled on a project-coloured tab: fill E0F3EC, outline 6BC7A4). Tab colours are per project in Visual Studio; the stock build applies the same recipe to the theme accent

EditorTabs.underlinedBorderColor.element: Selected document tab, outline: the active border token

EditorTabs.inactiveUnderlinedTabBackgrou.element: Quieter selected-tab fill after focus leaves the pane; readable with its native tab text

EditorTabs.inactiveUnderlinedTabBorderCo.element: Selected document tab when the editor is not focused, outline: VS's inactive border token (VS state not sampled)

Tree.selectionBackground.element: Selected row in a focused tree. Visual Studio marks it with a faint fill plus an accent pill that Rider cannot draw; the faint fill alone (E8EBED on F7FAFC) is too hard to find, so the accent tint recipe of the selected tab is used

ToolWindow.Header.inactiveBackground.element: Inactive header remains distinct from its pane body

ToolWindow.Header.background.element: Focused header in this theme's original hue

EditorTabs.underlinedTabForeground.element: Selected tab text: preserve this theme's foreground explicitly

List.selectionBackground.element: Explicit focused selection fill using this theme's own palette

Tree.selectionForeground.element: Focused file-selection text in this appearance's own palette

Tree.selectionInactiveBackground.element: Quieter file selection after focus leaves the project tree

ToolWindow.HeaderTab.underlinedTabForegr.element: Native tool-window tab text matches the focused editor-tab foreground

ToolWindow.HeaderTab.underlinedTabInacti.element: Native inactive tool-window tab text remains readable on the inactive fill

Tree.hash.element: Supported native project and structure tree guides
